info.name: Truv VOIE: Point-of-Sale Integration (Case Study)
info.description:
Income and employment verification (VOIE) embedded in a loan application point-of-sale, using Truv embedded orders. Modeled on the Truv and nCino point-of-sale experience. Written for the bank's developers: every request notes what it does, which fields to store and how they are used. Examples are real sandbox responses, with long arrays cut to 2 items and presigned URLs redacted.

Flow
0. One-time setup (server): POST /v1/webhooks/ to register your endpoint, GET /v1/webhooks/ to check it.
1. Employer search, optional (server): GET /v1/company-mappings-search/ to get a company_mapping_id for a deeplink.
2. Create order (server): POST /v1/orders/. Store id, user_id and bridge_token.
3. Launch Truv Bridge (browser, no API call): bridge.js with isOrder: true. Advance on onEvent COMPLETED from source order.
4. Receive webhooks (your endpoint): task-status-updated, order-status-updated, order-finalized. Verify X-WEBHOOK-SIGN.
5. Get order (server): GET /v1/orders/{order_id}/. Store voie_report_id.
6. VOIE report (server): GET /v1/users/{user_id}/reports/{report_id}/ as JSON or PDF. Optional POST /v1/users/{user_id}/reports/ for a fresh report.
7. Order lifecycle (server-side): GET /v1/orders/{order_id}/events/ for an audit trail, POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/ for a data refresh, POST /v1/orders/{order_id}/cancel/, GET /v1/orders/ to list and search.

Errors: Create order and Get order include real 400, 401, 403 and 404 examples. Folder 0 also has Delete webhook endpoint for cleanup.

Setup
1. Import this collection and the Truv Sandbox environment, then select the environment.
2. Fill truv_client_id and truv_secret with your SANDBOX keys from the Truv Dashboard (Development, API Keys). Never commit or share the secret.
3. Set webhook_url to your endpoint. Run folder 0 once.
4. Run folders 1 and 2. The test scripts store company_mapping_id, order_id, bridge_token, user_id and share_url.
5. Open share_url in a browser (or your own frontend with Bridge). Pick any sandbox payroll provider, for example ADP or Truv Payroll Provider, sign in with goodlogin / goodpassword, and enter 12345 if asked for an MFA code.
6. Watch the webhooks arrive at your endpoint, then run folders 5 and 6.

Webhook delivery: Truv expects a 2xx within 10 seconds and retries a failed delivery 3 times, 30 seconds apart.

Base URL is https://prod.truv.com/v1 for both sandbox and production. Your credentials decide which one you are in. Orders expire after a few days (see expired_at), so create a fresh order per borrower session.

item.name: 0. One-time setup
item.description:
Run once per environment (sandbox, then production), not per borrower.

Registers the bank's webhook endpoint with Truv so order and task events reach your backend. You can do the same in the Truv Dashboard under Development, then Webhooks. Use one method, not both, so each event is delivered once.

request.description:
What it does: tells Truv where to send webhooks and which events to send.

Body
- name: a label you will recognize in the Dashboard.
- webhook_url: your public HTTPS endpoint ({{webhook_url}}).
- events: task-status-updated (each connection's progress), order-status-updated (each employer on the order changes status), order-finalized (the order is final, no more data or refresh).
- env_type: sandbox, dev or prod. Must match the credentials you send.

Fields to store from the response
- id: the webhook ID. Keep it in config so you can PATCH /v1/webhooks/{id}/ (change URL or events, or set enabled: true after Truv disables a failing endpoint) or DELETE it.

Do not run this twice for the same URL. Each registration delivers its own copy of every event. Run List webhooks first to check.

What it does: lists the webhook endpoints registered for these credentials.

How to use it
- Check before registering, so you do not create a duplicate.
- Check enabled after an outage. Truv can disable an endpoint that keeps failing.

Nothing to store. The response is paginated (count, next, previous, results[]).

What it does: autocomplete search of Truv's employer directory. Matches on names, domains and synonyms, and tolerates typos.

Query parameters
- query (required): the employer name the borrower typed ({{employer_query}}).
- product_type: income, so success_rate reflects income verification.

Response: a list of matches. Each has company_mapping_id, name, domain, logo_url, success_rate (high, low, unsupported or null) and confidence_level (0 to 1).

Fields to store
- company_mapping_id of the employer the borrower picks. Pass it in employers[].company_mapping_id on Create order.

How to use it
- Call it from your backend as the borrower types (debounce), and show name and logo_url in a picker.
- If success_rate is low or unsupported, you can still create the order without the mapping and let the borrower choose another method in Bridge (for example document upload).

request.description:
Runs on the bank's backend, never in the browser, because it uses the API secret.

What it does: creates a verification order for one borrower. Truv returns a bridge_token that the frontend uses to open Truv Bridge.

Body fields used here (they match the prototype's app.py, plus the optional fields below)
- products: ["income"] for VOIE. Income includes employment data. Other options: ["assets"], ["income","assets"].
- first_name, last_name, email: the borrower from the application form.
- notification_settings.suppress_user_notifications: true. See the note below.
- external_user_id: your ID for the person (one value per borrower, never shared by a borrower and co-borrower). Lets Truv link that person's orders and supports data refresh.
- loan.application_number: the POS application number, used before a loan number exists. Use loan.loan_number once the LOS assigns one. Shows in the Truv Dashboard and on reports.
- employers[].company_mapping_id (optional): from Employer search. Bridge opens on that employer's login. The pre-request script removes employers when company_mapping_id is empty, so this request also works without folder 1.

Why notifications are suppressed
The borrower verifies inside the bank's application (embedded order), so a Truv email or SMS with a second link is not needed. In testing, orders created with an undeliverable email address went to status error because Truv could not deliver its notification. Suppressing notifications avoids that.

Alternative: delayed reminders
To nudge borrowers who leave Bridge unfinished, keep notifications on but delay them, for example notification_settings: {"suppress_user_notifications": false, "first_notification_delay_hours": 6}. Or create the order suppressed and send PATCH /v1/orders/{id}/ with suppress_user_notifications: false when the borrower closes Bridge without finishing. Truv then sends up to 3 reminders before the order expires. This needs a valid email or phone.

Other optional fields: phone, ssn (last 4 or 9 digits, improves matching), order_number, template_id (branding), loan originator and processor details.

Fields to store from the response, keyed to the loan application
- bridge_token (top level): pass to TruvBridge.init in the browser. Do not use employers[].bridge_token.
- id: the order ID. Used for Get order.
- user_id: arrives on every webhook. Use it to match events to the application. Also used for VOIE report calls.
- employers[].id: the suborder for each employer. Arrives as employer_id on order-status-updated and as tracking_info on task-status-updated.
- expired_at: create a new order if the borrower returns after this time.

share_url and short_share_url open the same order on a Truv-hosted page. Handy for testing without a frontend.

The test script saves order_id, bridge_token, user_id and share_url to the environment.

Errors seen in sandbox (saved as examples)
- 400 incorrect_parameters: a required field is missing. extra.invalid-params lists each field. Show a clear message to the loan officer, do not retry.
- 401 authentication_failed ("No such user"): the client ID is wrong or belongs to another environment.
- 403 not_authenticated: the client ID is valid but the secret is wrong. Check which key pair the server loaded. Neither 401 nor 403 should be retried.

item.name: 3. Launch Truv Bridge (browser, no API call)
4. Receive webhooks (your endpoint)
item.description:
Your backend exposes an HTTPS endpoint that Truv calls (registered in folder 0). The requests in this folder send real sandbox payloads to your own endpoint so you can test it. They do NOT call Truv.

Events for the VOIE flow, in the order they arrive
- task-status-updated: each step of a connection (login, mfa, parse, full_parse, done, or a failure such as login_error). Key fields: user_id, task_id, link_id, status, product, data_source, tracking_info (on orders this is the employers[].id).
- order-status-updated: an employer on the order changes status, for example completed. Key fields: user_id, order_id, employer_id, status, link_id.
- order-finalized: the whole order is final. No more data collection or refresh. Key fields: user_id, order_id.
- Also available: order-created, order-refresh-failed, order-batch-completed, certification-completed.

Verify every request
- Header X-WEBHOOK-SIGN is v1= followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the RAW request body, keyed with your Access Secret (not the client ID). Compute it over the raw bytes before parsing JSON, and compare in constant time.
- Reject a missing or wrong signature with 401.

Delivery rules
- Return a 2xx within 10 seconds. A failed or slow delivery is retried 3 times, 30 seconds apart.
- Respond fast and do the real work (Get order, report download) asynchronously.
- Match events to the application with user_id. Handle duplicates: webhook_id is unique per delivery.
- An endpoint that keeps failing can be disabled. Missed events are not replayed, so re-enable it (PATCH /v1/webhooks/{id}/ with enabled: true) and reconcile with Get order. GET /v1/webhook-requests/ shows the last 30 days of deliveries and their status codes.

Bridge's COMPLETED event can arrive before order-status-updated. In the sandbox run below, Bridge reported COMPLETED at 16:37:01 and order-status-updated arrived at 16:37:30. Advance the borrower on the Bridge event, and use the webhook to update the loan file.

Sends a real order-finalized payload, captured from a sandbox run, to {{webhook_url}} with an X-WEBHOOK-SIGN header computed from your secret. It does not call Truv.

When Truv sends it: once, when the whole order reaches its terminal state.

What your handler should do: mark the order final in the loan file. No more webhooks or data changes will come for this order.

In the body, user_id, order_id and employer_id are replaced with environment variables so your receiver matches the event to the order you just created. The payload exactly as Truv delivered it:

Runs on the bank's backend when the borrower finishes Bridge (onEvent COMPLETED from the order) or when order-status-updated reports completed.

What it does: returns the order with each employer's status, provider, employment, income, pay statements, W-2s and report IDs.

How to use it
- Before the borrower finishes, employers[].status is pending or sent and employments is null.
- After a successful verification, employers[].status is completed and completed_at is set.
- Map employments[] into the loan file: company.name, job_title, is_active, start_date, income and income_unit, pay_frequency, statements[] (gross_pay, net_pay, pay_date), annual_income_summary[], w2s[].

Fields to store
- voie_report_id: the VOIE report for underwriting (folder 6) and for Fannie Mae DU or Freddie Mac LPA (fannie_voie_report_id, freddie_voie_report_id).
- employers[].id and status: per-employer progress, matches employer_id on webhooks.
- completed_at: audit trail.
- employers[].pdf_report and statements[].file are short-lived presigned URLs. Download the files when you need them, do not store the URLs.

The test script saves employer_id and voie_report_id.

Examples: an order before Bridge is completed, and a completed sandbox order (arrays cut to 2 items, presigned URLs and link access token redacted).

404 {"detail": "Not found."}: no order with this ID for these credentials. Check the ID, and that the server uses the same key pair that created the order. Note the body shape differs from other Truv errors, which use error.code.

request.description:
What it does: the same report as a PDF (fmt=pdf; the default is fmt=json).

How to use it: save the file to the loan file or document system as the income verification document. The response is binary (Content-Type application/pdf). In Postman, use Send and Download. The sandbox report was about 24 KB.

Nothing else to store.

Optional. Orders already produce voie_report_id, so the standard flow does not need this call.

What it does: builds a new VOIE report from the borrower's current data, for example after a data refresh before closing.

Body
- is_voe: false for income and employment (VOIE). true for an employment-only VOE report.

Fields to store
- report_id: the new report. Use it in place of the earlier voie_report_id. Keep the earlier one for the audit trail.

The test script saves report_id to voie_report_id, so the two GET requests above fetch the new report.

Example: arrays cut to 2 items, presigned URLs redacted.

item.name: 7. Order lifecycle (server-side)
item.description:
Operations after the borrower finishes, or instead of finishing.

- Order events: audit trail for one order, for support tickets and QA.
- Data refresh: re-verify before closing without sending the borrower back through Bridge.
- Cancel: the borrower withdraws or the application is declined.
- List orders: reconciliation and back-office search, for example by application number.

Run these against a completed order. In a collection run they come last, so Cancel does not affect the earlier folders.

request.description:
What it does: returns the order's event history (created, employer completed, notification sent or failed, refresh orders).

Query
- include_refresh_orders: true to include events from refresh orders, flagged with is_refresh.

Use it for support: when a loan officer asks why an application is stuck, this shows whether the borrower logged in, which employer completed and whether any notification bounced. The example shows the original order plus a refresh, where Truv tried to email the borrower and delivery failed (example.com address).

request.description:
What it does: creates a new order that re-pulls data from the payroll connection the borrower already made. No Bridge session is needed while the link is still valid. Typical use: refresh income and employment just before closing.

Body
- products: income (or employment) for an income order.
- employers[].id: the employer to refresh, from Get order employers[].id ({{employer_id}}). Omit employers to refresh all.

Fields to store from the response
- id: the refresh order ID (stored as {{refresh_order_id}}). Poll it with Get order or wait for webhooks, as with the original.
- initial_order: points back to the original order. The original gets refresh_order set.
- user_id: unchanged, so webhooks match the same borrower.

Observed in sandbox
- The refresh finished within seconds with a new pdf_report and voie_report_id, but the employer status read error. Confirm with Truv which status to treat as final for refreshes.
- This endpoint has no notification_settings field, and Truv tried to email the borrower on the refresh (see Get order events). Confirm with Truv how to suppress notifications on refresh orders for an embedded flow.
